About Me

Engineer by passion,
builder by nature.

Hey there! My name is Krish, and I'm an undergraduate Electrical Engineering student at The University of Texas at Dallas with a passion for hands-on work, problem-solving, and technology. My interest in engineering started at a young age through building LEGO creations, designing Hot Wheels tracks, and constantly exploring how things worked. Over time, that curiosity grew into a passion for engineering real-world systems, which led me to pursue a career in electrical engineering.

Through my coursework and engineering experiences, I've developed a strong foundation in electrical engineering with hands-on exposure to hardware and wireless communication systems. During my co-op at Mobile Communications America, I contributed to RF and LTE/5G projects involving system testing, troubleshooting, and network optimization. As a member of Dallas Formula Racing, I've worked on the development of a Formula-style race car, focusing on PCB design, wire harness design, and system integration within a collaborative team environment. Through my involvement with IEEE, I've continued expanding my technical knowledge while also tutoring underclassmen in engineering courses I've previously completed.

My interests within electrical engineering span several industries, including automotive technology, semiconductor development, telecommunications, and wireless systems. I'm especially drawn to roles that involve designing and improving real-world hardware systems that drive innovation. I'm always excited to continue learning, take on new engineering challenges, and apply my skills to meaningful projects — so feel free to explore my work and see what I've been building.

  • Performed RF testing & verification of DAS networks — analyzed field RF data, optimized coverage through gain and power adjustments, identified signal degradation, and conducted onsite surveys for LTE/5G.
